import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

**What changed from the lead's report**

- **Sections:** I kept the lead's order, which already follows the questions a reader would ask. Headings are no longer numbered and contain only plain words, so links to them work. Where I shortened a heading, its dropped wording now opens the section, for example "**Does this rule out `#foo` tags? Yes — including the subtle variant.**"
- **Merged content:** the lead's opening paragraph listing its inputs now sits with the source list in "Sources and method".
- **Section references:** the lead's `§4`/`§7` references now link to the matching sections. I also added links from the bottom line, the adjusted requirements and the open questions to the sections behind them.
- **Checks:** the meaning is unchanged. A word-by-word comparison against `__final.md` found only those heading and link edits. Every table cell survives; two cells changed only because a `§` reference became a link.

**Diagrams accepted** (the manifest was ready and its source matched the lead's report):
- `import-escape` → `#figure-import-escape`, placed after the paragraph about how gcal currently wraps imported ALL-CAPS lines in bold. I split that paragraph from its "Flip it before the marker lands:" list so the figure could follow the paragraph that names the hazard.

No diagrams were omitted. Both are copied byte-for-byte and each sits in exactly one figure `<div>`. The lead's report had no Mermaid diagrams, so the file now has 2. Pandoc confirms every heading and figure anchor resolves.

**Links:** neither the lead's report nor the new file has any external URLs, so none needed checking and none are broken. Both relative image links point to files that exist next to the report.

- Reading the manifest by its label (`diagrams:…`) failed with `unknown_kind`, so I read it through its file reference (`file:explicit:ab3df2766c5f83ace4718675`).
